tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand the proxy's purpose: expose GitHub Copilot as both an OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic-compatible HTTP service. Skim the package manifest and TypeScript config to see the runtime stack (Bun, Hono, citty, tsdown, strict TS).

tour.title: CLI Entry Point
tour.description: src/main.ts wires the citty CLI and dispatches to four subcommands: start (run the proxy), auth (GitHub device-code login), check-usage (account quota report), debug (diagnose tokens / models). Read it first to see how every workflow is bootstrapped.

tour.title: HTTP Server and Middleware Stack
tour.description: src/server.ts builds the Hono app and the middleware chain in fixed order: traceIdMiddleware → logger → cors → createAuthMiddleware. Auth validates x-api-key or Authorization: Bearer (except for / and /usage-viewer). This is where every request lands before routing.

tour.title: Configuration and Mutable State
tour.description: config.ts owns the AppConfig shape and reads/writes ~/.local/share/copilot-api/config.json (or %USERPROFILE% on Windows; COPILOT_API_HOME overrides it). state.ts is the singleton holding live tokens, account type, rate-limit counters, and the model cache. Together they define what the running server knows about itself.

tour.title: GitHub Authentication Flow
tour.description: The auth subcommand drives a GitHub device-code OAuth flow: get-device-code starts it, poll-access-token waits for the user to approve, then the GitHub access token is exchanged for a Copilot bearer token used for upstream calls.

tour.title: Core Anthropic Path: /v1/messages Handler
tour.description: src/routes/messages/handler.ts is the brain of the Anthropic-compatible path. It runs in order: rate-limit → parse Anthropic payload → detect __SUBAGENT_MARKER__ (sets x-initiator: agent) → detect compact requests → force smallModel for warmup probes → merge mixed tool_result + text blocks → normalize the model id → pick one of three upstream flows.

tour.title: Preprocess and Effort Clamping
tour.description: preprocess.ts is the non-obvious transform step: it injects thinking: { type: 'adaptive' }, then clamps payload.output_config.effort to whatever the target model actually supports (e.g. opus-4.7 caps at 'medium'). This is why a config of 'high' can silently become 'medium' downstream — read it before debugging any reasoning-effort issue.

tour.title: Three Upstream Flows
tour.description: api-flows.ts dispatches to one of three upstream calls: handleWithMessagesApi (Copilot native /v1/messages, preferred for Claude), handleWithResponsesApi (Copilot /responses, for GPT models), and handleWithChatCompletions (fallback for everything else). All three support both streaming (SSE) and non-streaming, switching on payload.stream.

tour.title: OpenAI-Compatible Path
tour.description: src/routes/chat-completions/handler.ts mirrors the Anthropic flow for /v1/chat/completions, plus /v1/models lists the catalog (cached in state.ts via get-models.ts). This is the path most third-party OpenAI clients hit.

tour.title: Token Counting
tour.description: /v1/messages/count_tokens has two branches: when an anthropicApiKey is configured, Claude-family requests are forwarded to Anthropic's free /v1/messages/count_tokens endpoint for exact counts; otherwise we fall back to the GPT o200k_base tokenizer with a 1.15x multiplier as a safe overestimate.

tour.title: Usage Viewer and Debug
tour.description: /usage-viewer is an unauthenticated HTML dashboard backed by src/routes/usage/route.ts that surfaces quota and rate-limit info, and the debug subcommand prints the same data to the terminal. Useful for understanding what the proxy thinks about your account at any moment.

tour.title: Sticky Router (Out-of-Band Load Balancer)
tour.description: router/sticky-router.ts is a separate Bun process that accepts ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL traffic and load-balances across multiple copilot-api backends with a sticky-key strategy. It's what makes running several Copilot accounts in parallel transparent to Claude Code.

tour.title: Plugin Integrations: Subagent Marker
tour.description: Both plugins exist for one reason: stamp __SUBAGENT_MARKER__ into a <system-reminder> when a sub-agent starts, so the proxy can later flag the request with x-initiator: agent. claude-plugin/scripts/subagent-start-marker.js handles Claude Code; .opencode/plugins/subagent-marker.js handles Opencode. The matching parser is subagent-marker.ts on the proxy side.

tour.title: Delivery: Docker and CI
tour.description: Dockerfile builds a slim runtime image; .github/workflows/ci.yml runs lint + typecheck + tests on every push; release-docker.yml publishes images on tag. This is the production path the project actually ships through.

project.name: @jeffreycao/copilot-api
project.description: A reverse-engineered GitHub Copilot proxy that exposes Copilot capabilities through OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic-compatible HTTP APIs, plus CLI flows for authentication, startup, usage inspection, and debugging.

nodes.name: Runtime Bootstrap & Authentication
nodes.summary: This domain establishes local runtime state before the proxy can serve traffic. It covers GitHub device authentication, Copilot token acquisition, model caching, and startup-time environment preparation for the HTTP server.

businessRules: Authentication can reuse a cached GitHub token unless forced
Startup must ensure app paths and caches exist before serving traffic
Copilot token metadata can override inferred account type
crossDomainInteractions: Provides tokens, account metadata, and model inventory to request-routing domains
Feeds usage and debug domains with persisted token/runtime state

nodes.name: Anthropic Messages Proxying
nodes.summary: This domain handles the Anthropic-compatible /v1/messages path and decides how to translate or forward each request into Copilot backends. It contains the request preprocessing, model normalization, effort handling, and streaming/non-streaming dispatch rules that make Claude-facing traffic work against Copilot.

businessRules: Compact and tool-less probe traffic may be downgraded to a configured small model
Claude-native routing depends on supported endpoints and feature flags
Adaptive thinking effort must be clamped or retried when the backend rejects unsupported values
crossDomainInteractions: Depends on request governance before any upstream dispatch
Consumes runtime model cache and token state established during bootstrap
Shares token-estimation logic with the token accounting domain

nodes.name: OpenAI-Compatible Proxying
nodes.summary: This domain serves OpenAI-compatible request shapes, especially /v1/chat/completions, on top of GitHub Copilot APIs. It fills default limits, creates request/session identifiers, and preserves both streaming and non-streaming semantics for OpenAI-style clients.

businessRules: gpt-5.4 is rejected on the chat-completions path and must use /v1/responses or /v1/messages
Missing max_tokens is filled from model capability limits
Streaming responses must preserve SSE framing and premium accounting
crossDomainInteractions: Reuses runtime model cache from bootstrap
Is gated by the request governance domain before calling Copilot

nodes.name: Token Accounting
nodes.summary: This domain answers token-counting requests for Anthropic-compatible message payloads. It prefers Anthropic's exact count_tokens endpoint for Claude models when configured, then falls back to local translation and estimation with model-specific adjustments.

businessRules: Claude models use the real Anthropic count_tokens endpoint only when an API key is configured
Tool declarations may add synthetic system-prompt token overhead
Unknown models and handler failures fall back to input_tokens = 1
crossDomainInteractions: Uses model resolution rules from request-routing code
Reads configuration set during runtime bootstrap

nodes.name: Request Governance
nodes.summary: This domain enforces local operational controls before traffic reaches Copilot. It includes API key authentication, request throttling, and optional human approval for each proxied request.

businessRules: Unauthenticated access is allowed for only a small set of public paths such as / and /usage-viewer
When configured, rate limiting either waits or returns HTTP 429
Manual approval rejects requests with HTTP 403 when the operator declines
crossDomainInteractions: Gates Anthropic and OpenAI request flows
Relies on runtime config and mutable state initialized during bootstrap

nodes.name: Usage & Diagnostics
nodes.summary: This domain exposes operator-facing inspection tools for Copilot usage and local runtime health. It includes a CLI usage report, the browser-based usage viewer, and a debug command that reveals runtime, path, and token-presence information.

businessRules: Usage reporting requires a valid GitHub-authenticated session
The usage viewer page is intentionally public while the JSON usage API still reflects backend fetch success/failure
Debug output can be emitted as either plain text or JSON
crossDomainInteractions: Reads persisted token/runtime state from the bootstrap domain
Surfaces operational effects of request and authentication domains to operators

nodes.summary: The handler inspects compact-request markers and tool-less beta probe patterns, then may swap the request to the configured small model.

nodes.name: Sanitize Tools And Detect Subagent
nodes.summary: The handler removes or rewrites unsupported IDE tool declarations and extracts any embedded subagent marker from the first user turn.

nodes.name: Strip Boundaries And Merge Tool Results
nodes.summary: For non-compact requests, preprocessing removes synthetic tool-boundary text and merges mixed tool_result plus text blocks into a backend-friendly shape.

nodes.name: Normalize Model Id
nodes.summary: The proxy maps SDK-style Claude model IDs into Copilot endpoint IDs by extracting family/version patterns and looking for a matching cached model.

nodes.name: Resolve Effort And Dispatch
nodes.summary: The handler logs the effective effort source, optionally requests manual approval, and dispatches to native messages, responses, or chat-completions based on model support.

nodes.name: Prepare Native Messages Payload
nodes.summary: Before calling Copilot's native messages endpoint, preprocessing strips unsupported cache_control fields, filters invalid thinking blocks, and enables adaptive thinking when the selected model supports it.

nodes.name: Build Enhanced Native Payload
nodes.summary: The native request builder removes top_p, forces temperature=1, and supplies adaptive-thinking output_config effort defaults when the model supports them.

nodes.name: Resolve Beta And Request Headers
nodes.summary: The native messages path filters incoming anthropic-beta values through a safe allowlist and adds Copilot-aligned beta headers when model capabilities require them.

nodes.name: Retry On Invalid Effort
nodes.summary: If Copilot rejects the configured reasoning effort, the proxy parses supported values from the backend error and retries with a downgraded effort.

nodes.name: Retry On Thinking Block Errors
nodes.summary: If native messages reject modified thinking signatures, the proxy strips assistant thinking blocks and retries once with a safer payload.

nodes.name: Stream Or Return Native Response
nodes.summary: After createMessages returns, the proxy either passes through SSE with response headers adjusted for streaming or returns the native JSON body for non-streaming requests.

nodes.name: Check Rate Limit
nodes.summary: The chat-completions handler applies the shared request-throttling check before any payload processing begins.

nodes.name: Validate Model Endpoint
nodes.summary: The handler looks up the selected model and rejects gpt-5.4 on this endpoint, directing callers to /v1/responses or /v1/messages instead.

nodes.name: Approve And Default Max Tokens
nodes.summary: If manual approval is enabled the request must be confirmed, and missing max_tokens is filled from the selected model's max_output_tokens limit.

nodes.name: Create Copilot Chat Request
nodes.summary: The proxy generates request/session IDs and forwards the normalized payload to Copilot's chat completions backend.

nodes.name: Stream Or Return Chat Response
nodes.summary: The handler either returns a JSON completion or relays SSE chunks while logging premium metadata for the completed request.

nodes.name: Parse Token Count Request
nodes.summary: The count-tokens handler reads the Anthropic payload and first tries the exact Anthropic counting path for eligible Claude models.

nodes.name: Forward Claude Count To Anthropic
nodes.summary: When an Anthropic API key exists, Claude-family token counting is forwarded to the real /v1/messages/count_tokens endpoint with dotted model names converted to dash form.

nodes.name: Translate And Resolve Fallback Model
nodes.summary: If exact counting is unavailable, the handler translates the payload to an OpenAI-like shape and resolves the endpoint model used for local estimation.

nodes.name: Apply Tool Overhead And Claude Multiplier
nodes.summary: Local estimation adds tool-system overhead for eligible requests and multiplies Claude totals by the configured token multiplier before returning the final count.

nodes.name: Return Estimate Or Safe Fallback
nodes.summary: The handler returns the final token count when possible, but falls back to input_tokens=1 for unknown models or unexpected errors.

nodes.name: Install Auth Middleware
nodes.summary: The Hono server installs auth middleware globally while explicitly exempting / and /usage-viewer paths from authentication.

nodes.name: Bypass Public Paths And Options
nodes.summary: The middleware lets OPTIONS requests and configured public paths pass through without credential checks.

nodes.name: Extract Api Key Or Bearer
nodes.summary: Protected requests may authenticate with x-api-key or Authorization: Bearer, and the middleware normalizes both forms into one comparable key.

nodes.name: Accept Or Reject Request
nodes.summary: When configured API keys exist, the middleware either continues the request or returns a 401 authentication_error response.

nodes.name: Compute Throttle Window
nodes.summary: The shared rate-limit helper compares the current request timestamp against the last forwarded request and the configured interval.

nodes.name: Reject On Rate Limit Exceed
nodes.summary: If the throttle window is still active and waiting is disabled, the helper returns an HTTP 429 error immediately.

nodes.name: Wait When Throttle Is Configured To Block
nodes.summary: When wait mode is enabled, the proxy sleeps for the remaining window and only then updates the request timestamp and proceeds.

nodes.name: Prompt Manual Approval
nodes.summary: If manual approval mode is enabled, the operator must confirm the request or the proxy returns HTTP 403.

nodes.name: Render Usage Report
nodes.summary: The CLI prints the quota summary in a terminal box and exits with an error status if usage retrieval fails.

nodes.name: Serve Usage Viewer Html
nodes.summary: The HTTP server exposes /usage-viewer as a static HTML page read from pages/index.html so operators can inspect usage in a browser.

nodes.name: Redirect Trailing Slash
nodes.summary: The server normalizes /usage-viewer/ to /usage-viewer to keep the viewer entry URL consistent.

nodes.name: Serve Usage Json
nodes.summary: The backing /usage endpoint fetches the latest Copilot usage snapshot and returns JSON or a 500 error payload.

nodes.name: Collect Package Version
nodes.summary: The debug command reads package.json to determine the installed copilot-api version, falling back to unknown when unavailable.

nodes.name: Capture Runtime And Path Info
nodes.summary: Runtime name, runtime version, platform, architecture, and application paths are collected into the debug payload.

nodes.name: Detect Token File Presence
nodes.summary: The debug flow checks whether the GitHub token file exists and contains non-empty content.

nodes.name: Emit Debug Output
nodes.summary: Finally, the command aggregates the debug payload and prints it either as pretty plain text or as structured JSON.

edges.description: Startup and auth populate githubToken, copilotToken, account type, and model cache consumed by the /v1/messages routing path.
Chat-completions routing depends on the same runtime token state and cached model inventory loaded during startup.
Token counting reuses configured Anthropic credentials and model metadata initialized from runtime configuration and bootstrap.
Rate limiting and manual approval run before Anthropic-compatible requests are forwarded upstream.
The same governance controls guard OpenAI-compatible chat-completions requests.
Both domains share Anthropic payload semantics, model resolution rules, and Claude-specific token/effort behaviors.
Usage and debug tooling inspect persisted token files, runtime paths, and authenticated Copilot session state created by bootstrap/auth flows.
